changes.before: Section318 permits the specified IEEPA203/205 implementation powers, regulations, licences and orders and imports206(b)/(c) penalties for violations as printed.
changes.after: Section 318(a) permits the President to exercise the specified IEEPA 203/205 implementation authorities; 318(b) requires the President to issue regulations, licences and orders necessary to carry out the title; 318(c) imports 206(b)/(c) penalties for violations as printed.

changes.before: passed disapproval adds12calendar days of presidential consideration and veto adds10calendar days; enacted disapproval prohibits the action.
changes.after: a covered joint resolution of disapproval passing both Houses in accordance with 321(c) prohibits the proposed action for 12 calendar days after the date of passage. If that covered resolution passes both Houses under 321(c) and the President vetoes it, the President may not take the proposed action for 10 calendar days after the date of the President's veto. These event-anchored periods are not automatically cumulative extensions; enacted disapproval prohibits the action.

source_points.passage: SEC. 318. IMPLEMENTATION; REGULATIONS; PENALTIES. (a) Implementation.--The President may exercise all authorities provided to the President under sections 203 and 205 of the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (50 U.S.C. 1702 and 1704) to carry out this title.
(b) Regulations.--The President shall issue such regulations, licenses, and orders as are necessary to carry out this title.

(4) Limitation on actions during presidential consideration of a joint resolution of disapproval.--Notwithstanding any other provision of law, if a joint resolution of disapproval relating to a report submitted under subsection (a)(1) proposing an action described in subsection (a)(2) passes both Houses of Congress in accordance with subsection (c), the President may not take that action for a period of 12 calendar days after the date of passage of the joint resolution of disapproval.

(5) Limitation on actions during congressional reconsideration of a joint resolution of disapproval.-- Notwithstanding any other provision of law, if a joint resolution of disapproval relating to a report submitted under subsection (a)(1) proposing an action described in subsection (a)(2) passes both Houses of Congress in accordance with subsection (c), and the President vetoes the joint resolution, the President may not take that action for a period of 10 calendar days after the date of the President's veto.
